html:
The Chickahominy are a Native American people of the Chickahominy River, between the James and York rivers in eastern Virginia. They spoke an Algonquian language and farmed maize along the river.

Unusually, they stayed outside the paramount chiefdom of Powhatan, though they often allied with it, and were governed by a council of elders rather than a single chief. In 1607 Powhatan's brother Opechancanough captured John Smith of Jamestown near their river. The Chickahominy traded corn to the hungry colonists and in 1614 made a treaty of alliance with the English. As the colony grew they lost their land and moved several times. They held their community together through the segregation era, and in 2018 the Chickahominy won federal recognition along with five other Virginia tribes, among them the Rappahannock and the Monacan.
